[LGRA.10.3.4] **The action-argument inventory is closed.** Each action verb
accepts exactly the language-defined kwargs and flags below, plus — where the
verb has one — the kwargs of its user-declared namespace. Any other kwarg name
is a compile error `DS_VALIDATE_BAD_KWARG`; any other flag name is
`DS_VALIDATE_BAD_FLAG`. [LGRA.10.3.3] is the *action's contract* that
[LGRA.10.3.2] delegates validity to, and is its single normative home.

The two kwarg namespaces cannot collide: [LLEX.9.5] reserves `retain`,
`cooldown`, `nocooldown` and `as` against use as an author binding target, so a
language-defined modifier is never also a slot or service kwarg.

`as` is **not** an action argument — it is a trailing clause of `call_action`
([LGRA.10.1]) rather than an `action_arg`, and appears above only where a row
would otherwise read as excluding it.

A verb whose user-declared namespace is `—` takes a **fixed** argument list, and
that is exactly the case in which nothing else in the corpus narrows the
grammar: [LGRA.10.1] admits `action_arg*` after every head, so for those verbs
this clause is the only thing that closes the set.
